newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-CFM sale bill tabled in Australian parliament.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-CFM sale bill tabled in Australian parliament.

text.p: Australian Finance Minister John Fahey introduced into the lower house of parliament on Thursday legislation to privatise the government's funds management arm.
But debate on the Commonwealth Funds Management Ltd (CFM) Sale Bill, which has A$8.0 billion in funds under management, was adjourned.
A government spokesman later told Reuters the bill was expected to pass through the lower house and into the upper house Senate during the next sitting period, which begins on October 8.
The bill is not expected to face opposition in the Senate, where the government needs two extra votes to pass any legislation.
However, a Labor Party spokesman said the opposition was considering an amendment, under which it would be specified that the sale proceeds would be used to repay government debt.

"Given the government's policy in regards to the funds raised from asset sales, we would have thought it would be a strong requirement that the government make a commitment to use those funds to retire debt," the spokesman told Reuters.
CFM is expected to sell for about A$100 million.
The Australian government announced plans to sell CFM in May this year and called for expressions of interest on August 8.
Lend Lease Corp Ltd, ING Bank unit Mercantile Mutual, and Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd are among potential bidders for CFM.
